fullPassage: Countershading is the process of optical flattening that provides camouflage to animals. When sunlight illuminates an object from above, the object will be brightest on top. The color of the object will gradually shade darker toward the bottom. This shading gives the object depth and allows the viewer to distinguish its shape. Thus even if an animal is exactly, but uniformly, the same color as the substrate, it will be easily visible when illuminated. Most animals, however, are darker above than they are below. When they are illuminated from above, the darker back is lightened and the lighter belly is shaded. The animal thus appears to be a single color and easily blends in with the substrate. This pattern of coloration, or countershading, reduces the visual impression of shape in the organism. It allows the animal to blend in with its background. What exactly does normal science involve? According to Thomas Kuhn it is primarily a matter of puzzle-solving. However successful a paradigm is, it will always encounter certain problems — phenomena which it cannot easily accommodate, or mismatches between the theory's predictions and the experimental facts. The job of the normal scientist is to try to eliminate these minor puzzles while making as few changes as possible to the paradigm. So normal science is a conservative activity — its practitioners are not trying to make any earth-shattering discoveries, but rather just to develop and extend the existing paradigm. In Kuhn's words, 'normal science does not aim at novelties of fact or theory, and when successful finds none'. Above all, Kuhn stressed that normal scientists are not trying to test the paradigm. On the contrary, they accept the paradigm unquestioningly, and conduct their research within the limits it sets. If a normal scientist gets an experimental result which conflicts with the paradigm, they will usually assume that their experimental technique is faulty, not that the paradigm is wrong. Journalists hold knowledge, but it is not theoretical in nature: one might argue that the public depends on journalists in the same way that patients depend on doctors, but in practice a journalist can serve the public usually only by working for a news organization, which can fire her or him at will. Journalists' income depends not on the public, but on the employing news organization, which often derives the large majority of its revenue from advertisers. He tells the story of a day care center in Israel that decided to fine parents who arrived late to pick up their children, in the hope that this would discourage them from doing so. In fact, the exact opposite happened. Before the imposition of fines, parents felt guilty about arriving late, and guilt was effective in ensuring that only a few did so. Once a fine was introduced, it seems that in the minds of the parents the entire scenario was changed from a social contract to a market one. Essentially, they were paying for the center to look after their children after hours. Some parents thought it worth the price, and the rate of late arrivals increased. Significantly, once the center abandoned the fines and went back to the previous arrangement, late arrivals remained at the high level they had reached during the period of the fines. The right to be forgotten is a right distinct from but related to a right to privacy. The right to privacy is, among other things, the right for information traditionally regarded as protected or personal not to be revealed. The right to be forgotten, in contrast, can be applied to information that has been in the public domain. The right to be forgotten broadly includes the right of an individual not to be forever defined by information from a specific point in time. One motivation for such a right is to allow individuals to move on with their lives and not be defined by a specific event or period in their lives. For example, it has long been recognized in some countries, such as the UK and France, that even past criminal convictions should eventually be "spent" and not continue to affect a person's life. Despite the reason for supporting the right to be forgotten, the right to be forgotten can sometimes come into conflict with other rights. For example, formal exceptions are sometimes made for security or public health reasons. There is no doubt that the length of some literary works is overwhelming. Reading or translating a work in class, hour after hour, week after week, can be such a boring experience that many students never want to open a foreign language book again. Extracts provide one type of solution. The advantages are obvious: reading a series of passages from different works produces more variety in the classroom, so that the teacher has a greater chance of avoiding monotony, while still giving learners a taste at least of an author's special flavour. On the other hand, a student who is only exposed to 'bite-sized chunks' will never have the satisfaction of knowing the overall pattern of a book, which is after all the satisfaction most of us seek when we read something in our own language. Moreover, there are some literary features that cannot be adequately illustrated by a short excerpt: the development of plot or character, for instance, with the gradual involvement of the reader that this implies; or the unfolding of a complex theme through the juxtaposition of contrasting views. In the past, it was often assumed that competence acquired in the first language (L1) was qualitatively different from that in a second language (L2) or any subsequent language. This privileging of the "native language" led to many popular misconceptions, such as believing that children of bilingual parents would never fully acquire either language, remaining somehow linguistically disadvantaged. Such claims are due to the belief that monolingualism is the norm, and they are held by many in the United States and other countries where a single language is politically or socially dominant. That this view must be wrong can easily be seen from the fact that many people in the world are speaking more than one language. In fact, it is bilingualism or trilingualism rather than monolingualism that is most common. Even in supposedly monolingual nations like the United States, U.S. Census figures from 2014 showed that at least 20 percent of the population regularly spoke a language other than English, and 53 percent of these people also spoke English. From Descartes to the present, reason has been prized in Western culture, standing as the chief virtue of the modernist world-view. As we are led to believe, it is the power to reason that sets humans above the remainder of the animal kingdom, and is essential for human survival. Literary study suggests otherwise. Among the most important objections are those of the French literary theorist Jacques Derrida. Derrida's writings, often identified as deconstructionist, are ambiguous and open to many interpretations. From one perspective, however, they significantly undermine the cultural investment in human reason. Consider two major premises. First, suggests Derrida, rational arguments bring about a massive suppression of meaning. Broadly put, when we are convinced by a rational argument we do not know more, but less. Second, if closely examined, all rational arguments will collapse. Rationality, then, is not a foundation for anything — for our institutions of government and science, for example, or as a way of deciding on what is moral or worthwhile. Rather, Derrida suggests, our 'good reasons' are in the end both suppressive and empty. How the children learn new concepts? The traditional view of conceptual change was that new learned theories replace old ones: once a children learns that the Earth rotates around the sun, their previous theory (based on their experience of seeing the sun move) that the sun rotates around the Earth, would be overwritten. Recent evidence from adults suggests something more surprising: that these old, incorrect theories remain stored in the brain; often we still need them to drive our perceptual expectations such as where to look for the sun in the sky. But in an educational context, we need inhibitory control to suppress them in order to reach the newer, correct theories. The naive incorrect theory is more familiar and automatic; the new theory need time and deliberate suppression of the old theory to be actively retrieved. Copying is pedestrian. Copying is peculiar. On the one hand, copying makes us what we are. Our bodies take shape from the transcription of protein templates, our languages from the mimicry of privileged sounds, our crafts from the repetition of prototypes. Cultures hold together in the faithful transmission of rituals and rules of conduct. To copy cell for cell, word for word, image for image, is to make the known world our own. On the other hand, we are not identical, nor do we wish to think of ourselves as clones. Copying is ultimately imperfect, our errors eventually our heirs. The more widespread the act of copying, the greater the likelihood of significant mistranscription. Genetic slip or evolution, written mistake or midrash, miscopying raises hard questions about identity, security, and integrity. The same technical advances that make our skill at copying so impressive also intensify the dilemmas of forgery. We use copies to certify originals, originals to certify copies, then we stand confused. While discussions of human credulity often portray children as being highly credulous, experiments show that young children already use sophisticated methods for deciding whom to trust. In some such experiments, children interact with two individuals who give different names to previously unfamiliar objects. The child must decide whom to believe. In general, from an early age children would choose to believe a person they have a strong relationship with over a stranger. At age three, they would still do this even if the familiar person has a history of having given names to objects that the child recognized to be wrong. By age five, though, they will give more credence to a relative stranger who has some history of having been accurate than to a familiar person with a record of inaccuracy. What happens if there are two strangers to choose between with similar records of accuracy? Then the stranger who comes from the same cultural group as the child, as determined by accent, for example, is the one believed. Experiments have also been done on adults, who, like children, use information about the source of theories to decide whether to adopt them. We tend to follow opinion leaders, people in authority and those whose beliefs we share. Similar experiments show that among chimpanzees, those with higher status are trusted more. We all need ways of deciding whom to believe. Evolution has provided us and other species a start.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) brightest=가장 밝은, (B) lightened=밝아지다, (C) reduces=줄이다
det.analysis:
✅ ① brightest — lightened — reduces: 원문 일치. 위에서 빛이 비치면 물체 윗부분이 가장 '밝고(brightest)', 역광 음영에서는 어두운 등이 '밝아지며(lightened)', 이 무늬가 형태 인상을 '줄인다(reduces)'는 흐름에 부합
❌ ② darkest — lightened — reduces: (A) darkest(가장 어두운)는 윗부분이 가장 밝다는 원문과 반대
❌ ③ brightest — darkened — reduces: (B) darkened(어두워지다)는 어두운 등이 '밝아진다'는 원문과 반대
❌ ④ brightest — lightened — increases: (C) increases(늘리다)는 형태 인상을 '줄인다'는 원문과 정반대
det.tip: brightest on top(가장 밝음) + darker back is lightened(밝아짐) + reduces the visual impression of shape(줄임)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② 원문은 widespread(널리 퍼진). 자유시장이 최선의 체제로 받아들여지고 널리 채택돼 왔다는 맥락이므로 limited(제한된)는 부적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① best — 자본주의·자유시장이 자원 배분의 '최선의(best)' 체제로 받아들여진다는 맥락에 적절
✅ ② limited — 원문은 widespread(널리 퍼진). 앞에서 여러 나라가 자유시장으로 전면 전환하거나 그 요소를 채택했다고 했으므로 그 수용은 '널리 퍼진' 것이다. limited(제한된)로 바꾸면 정반대가 되어 부적절 ← 정답
❌ ③ many — 정부 개입이 여러(many) 형태를 띤다는 맥락에 적절
❌ ④ important — 경기 순환을 통제하려는 시도가 '가장 중요한(important)' 개입 형태라는 맥락에 적절
det.tip: 자유시장은 최선의 체제로 받아들여져 왔으므로 그 수용은 the widespread acceptance(널리 퍼진 수용)이며, limited로 바꾸면 논리가 무너진다

det.korean: their clients are dependent on them = 의뢰인이 전문가에게 '의존하는'

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 discourage와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: discourage = 단념시키다, 막다 → deter(단념시키다)
det.analysis:
❌ ① encourage — '장려하다'. discourage와 정반대 의미

questions.stem: 다음 영영 풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "a situation in which there is not enough of something that is needed"

det.korean: shortage = 부족 (필요한 것이 충분치 않은 상태)
det.analysis:
✅ ① shortage — '부족'. 필요한 것이 충분하지 않은 상태라는 영영 풀이에 정확히 대응 (본문: product or service shortages) ← 정답
❌ ② surplus — '잉여, 과잉'. 오히려 남는 상태로 풀이와 정반대
❌ ③ revenue — '수익'. 벌어들이는 돈을 뜻해 풀이와 무관
❌ ④ demand — '수요'. 원하는 양을 뜻해 '부족'과 다름
det.tip: not enough of something that is needed = 필요한 것의 부족 = shortage

✅ ④ courage — '용기'. 대부분의 사람이 '나설 용기가 없다'는 것이 문제이고, 그래서 요다를 안전장치로 삼아 솔직히 말하게 한다는 흐름에 정확히 부합 ← 정답
det.tip: most people don't have the courage to speak up = 나설 용기가 없다

questions.passage: The right to be forgotten is a right <u>distinct</u> from but related to a right to privacy. The right to privacy is, among other things, the right for information traditionally regarded as protected or personal not to be revealed. The right to be forgotten, in contrast, can be applied to information that has been in the public domain. The right to be forgotten broadly includes the right of an individual not to be forever defined by information from a specific point in time. One motivation for such a right is to allow individuals to move on with their lives and not be defined by a specific event or period in their lives. For example, it has long been recognized in some countries, such as the UK and France, that even past criminal convictions should eventually be "spent" and not continue to affect a person's life. Despite the reason for supporting the right to be forgotten, the right to be forgotten can sometimes come into conflict with other rights. For example, formal exceptions are sometimes made for security or public health reasons.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 distinct와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: distinct from = ~와 구별되는, 별개의 → separate(별개의)
det.analysis:
✅ ① separate — '별개의, 구별되는'. 잊힐 권리가 사생활 권리와 '구별되지만(distinct)' 관련된다는 맥락에 가장 가까운 동의어 ← 정답
❌ ② identical — '동일한'. distinct와 정반대
❌ ③ derived — '파생된'. 구별된다는 의미와 다름
❌ ④ hidden — '숨겨진'. 문맥과 무관
det.tip: a right distinct from but related to = 구별되지만 관련된 ≒ separate

questions.passage: There is no doubt that the length of some literary works is overwhelming. Reading or translating a work in class, hour after hour, week after week, can be such a boring experience that many students never want to open a foreign language book again. Extracts provide one type of solution. The advantages are obvious: reading a series of passages from different works produces more variety in the classroom, so that the teacher has a greater chance of avoiding <u>monotony</u>, while still giving learners a taste at least of an author's special flavour. On the other hand, a student who is only exposed to 'bite-sized chunks' will never have the satisfaction of knowing the overall pattern of a book, which is after all the satisfaction most of us seek when we read something in our own language. Moreover, there are some literary features that cannot be adequately illustrated by a short excerpt: the development of plot or character, for instance, with the gradual involvement of the reader that this implies; or the unfolding of a complex theme through the juxtaposition of contrasting views.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 monotony와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: monotony = 단조로움 ↔ diversity(다양성)
det.analysis:
❌ ① boredom — '지루함'. monotony와 비슷한 뜻이라 반의어가 아님
✅ ② diversity — '다양성'. 여러 작품의 발췌를 읽어 '단조로움(monotony)'을 피한다는 맥락에서 monotony와 반대되는 뜻 ← 정답
❌ ③ tedium — '지루함, 따분함'. monotony의 유의어라 반대가 아님
❌ ④ uniformity — '획일성, 한결같음'. 단조로움과 비슷한 뜻으로 반의어가 아님
det.tip: avoiding monotony(단조로움) ↔ diversity(다양성)

questions.passage: How the children learn new concepts? The traditional view of conceptual change was that new learned theories replace old ones: once a children learns that the Earth rotates around the sun, their previous theory (based on their experience of seeing the sun move) that the sun rotates around the Earth, would be overwritten. Recent evidence from adults suggests something more surprising: that these old, incorrect theories __________ in the brain; often we still need them to drive our perceptual expectations such as where to look for the sun in the sky. But in an educational context, we need inhibitory control to suppress them in order to reach the newer, correct theories. The naive incorrect theory is more familiar and automatic; the new theory need time and deliberate suppression of the old theory to be actively retrieved.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: old, incorrect theories remain stored in the brain = 오래된 오개념이 뇌에 계속 저장되어 남아 있다
det.analysis:
❌ ① quickly disappear — '빠르게 사라진다'. 뒤에서 '우리는 여전히 그것들이 필요하다'고 하므로 사라진다는 것은 모순
❌ ② are fully erased — '완전히 지워진다'. 오개념이 남아 있다는 최신 증거와 반대
✅ ③ remain stored — '저장된 채 남아 있다'. 최신 증거에 따르면 오래된 오개념이 뇌에 '그대로 남아' 지각적 기대를 이끄는 데 여전히 쓰인다는 흐름에 정확히 부합 ← 정답
❌ ④ become correct — '옳게 바뀐다'. 오개념이 그대로 남는다는 내용과 어긋남
det.tip: old, incorrect theories remain stored in the brain; often we still need them

questions.passage: But in an educational context, we need inhibitory control to suppress them in order to reach the newer, correct theories. The naive incorrect theory is more familiar and automatic; the new theory need time and deliberate suppression of the old theory to be actively _____.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 문맥과 어법에 맞는 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오. (retrieve)

det.korean: to be actively retrieved = 능동적으로 '인출되기' 위해 (수동 부정사)
det.analysis:
빈칸은 'to be actively _____' 구조로 'to be + 과거분사'의 수동 부정사 자리이다. 새(올바른) 이론은 낡은 이론을 억제해야 비로소 '인출되는(retrieved)' 대상이므로 동사 retrieve의 과거분사 retrieved가 알맞다.

원문: 'the new theory need time and deliberate suppression of the old theory to be actively retrieved'

새 이론은 시간과 의도적 억제를 거쳐야 능동적으로 인출된다는 의미이다.
det.tip: to be + p.p.(수동 부정사) → retrieve → retrieved

questions.passage: Our bodies take shape from the transcription of protein templates, our languages from the mimicry of privileged sounds, our crafts from the repetition of prototypes. Cultures hold together in the faithful _____ of rituals and rules of conduct.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 문맥과 어법에 맞는 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오. (transmit)

det.korean: the faithful transmission of rituals = 의식의 충실한 '전달'(명사)
det.analysis:
빈칸은 형용사 faithful의 수식을 받고 뒤에 전치사구 of rituals and rules of conduct가 이어지는 '명사' 자리이다. 따라서 동사 transmit의 명사형 transmission이 알맞다.

원문: 'Cultures hold together in the faithful transmission of rituals and rules of conduct'

문화는 의식과 행동 규범의 '충실한 전달'을 통해 유지된다는 의미이다.
det.tip: 형용사(faithful) + ___ + of ~ → 명사 자리 → transmit → transmission

questions.passage: Copying is pedestrian. Copying is peculiar. On the one hand, copying makes us what we are. Our bodies take shape from the transcription of protein templates, our languages from the mimicry of privileged sounds, our crafts from the repetition of prototypes. Cultures hold together in the faithful transmission of rituals and rules of conduct. To copy cell for cell, word for word, image for image, is to make the known world our own. On the other hand, we are not identical, nor do we wish to think of ourselves as clones. Copying is ultimately imperfect, our errors eventually our heirs. The more widespread the act of copying, the greater the likelihood of significant mistranscription. Genetic slip or evolution, written mistake or midrash, miscopying raises hard questions about identity, security, and integrity. The same technical advances that make our skill at copying so impressive also intensify the dilemmas of forgery. We use copies to certify originals, originals to certify copies, then we __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: then we stand confused = 그러다 우리는 결국 '혼란스러운 채로 있게' 된다
det.analysis:
❌ ① feel confident — '자신감을 느낀다'. 복제와 원본이 서로를 인증하는 역설적 상황과 어울리지 않음
❌ ② reject both — '둘 다 거부한다'. 본문은 거부가 아니라 혼란을 말함
❌ ③ move forward — '앞으로 나아간다'. 혼란에 빠진다는 결론과 어긋남
✅ ④ stand confused — '혼란스러운 채로 있다'. 복제로 원본을 인증하고 원본으로 복제를 인증하다 보니 결국 무엇이 진짜인지 '혼란스러워진다'는 결론에 정확히 부합 ← 정답
det.tip: use copies to certify originals, originals to certify copies, then we stand confused(혼란)

questions.passage: While discussions of human credulity often portray children as being highly credulous, experiments show that young children already use <u>sophisticated</u> methods for deciding whom to trust. In some such experiments, children interact with two individuals who give different names to previously unfamiliar objects. The child must decide whom to believe. In general, from an early age children would choose to believe a person they have a strong relationship with over a stranger. At age three, they would still do this even if the familiar person has a history of having given names to objects that the child recognized to be wrong. By age five, though, they will give more credence to a relative stranger who has some history of having been accurate than to a familiar person with a record of inaccuracy. What happens if there are two strangers to choose between with similar records of accuracy? Then the stranger who comes from the same cultural group as the child, as determined by accent, for example, is the one believed. Experiments have also been done on adults, who, like children, use information about the source of theories to decide whether to adopt them. We tend to follow opinion leaders, people in authority and those whose beliefs we share. Similar experiments show that among chimpanzees, those with higher status are trusted more. We all need ways of deciding whom to believe. Evolution has provided us and other species a start.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 sophisticated와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: sophisticated = 정교한, 고도의 → advanced(고도의, 정교한)
det.analysis:
✅ ① advanced — '고도의, 정교한'. 어린아이가 누구를 믿을지 정하는 데 이미 '정교한(sophisticated)' 방법을 쓴다는 맥락에 가장 가까운 동의어 ← 정답
❌ ② simple — '단순한'. sophisticated와 정반대
❌ ③ honest — '정직한'. 방법의 정교함과 무관한 속성
❌ ④ random — '무작위의'. 정교함과 반대 방향
det.tip: use sophisticated methods = 정교한 방법을 쓰다 ≒ advanced

questions.passage: While discussions of human credulity often portray children as being highly credulous, experiments show that young children already use sophisticated methods for deciding whom to trust. In some such experiments, children interact with two individuals who give different names to previously unfamiliar objects. The child must decide whom to believe. In general, from an early age children would choose to believe a person they have a (A)[weak / strong] relationship with over a stranger. At age three, they would still do this even if the familiar person has a history of having given names to objects that the child recognized to be wrong. By age five, though, they will give more credence to a relative stranger who has some history of having been (B)[accurate / inaccurate] than to a familiar person with a record of inaccuracy. What happens if there are two strangers to choose between with similar records of accuracy? Then the stranger who comes from the same cultural group as the child, as determined by accent, for example, is the one believed. Experiments have also been done on adults, who, like children, use information about the source of theories to decide whether to adopt them. We tend to follow opinion leaders, people in authority and those whose beliefs we share. Similar experiments show that among chimpanzees, those with (C)[higher / lower] status are trusted more. We all need ways of deciding whom to believe. Evolution has provided us and other species a start.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) strong=강한, (B) accurate=정확한, (C) higher=더 높은
det.analysis:
❌ ① weak — accurate — higher: (A) weak(약한)는 아이가 '강한' 관계를 맺은 사람을 믿는다는 원문과 반대
✅ ② strong — accurate — higher: 원문 일치. 아이는 '강한(strong)' 관계의 사람을 믿고, 다섯 살엔 '정확했던(accurate)' 낯선 이를 더 신뢰하며, 침팬지도 '더 높은(higher)' 지위를 더 신뢰한다는 흐름에 부합 ← 정답
❌ ③ strong — inaccurate — higher: (B) inaccurate(부정확한)는 '정확했던' 낯선 이를 더 믿는다는 원문과 반대
❌ ④ strong — accurate — lower: (C) lower(더 낮은)는 '더 높은' 지위가 더 신뢰받는다는 원문과 정반대
det.tip: a strong relationship + history of having been accurate + higher status are trusted more

questions.passage: What exactly does normal science involve? According to Thomas Kuhn it is primarily a matter of puzzle-solving. However successful a paradigm is, it will always encounter certain problems — phenomena which it cannot easily accommodate, or mismatches between the theory's predictions and the experimental facts. The job of the normal scientist is to try to ①<u>eliminate</u> these minor puzzles while making as few changes as possible to the paradigm. So normal science is a ②<u>conservative</u> activity — its practitioners are not trying to make any earth-shattering discoveries, but rather just to develop and extend the existing paradigm. In Kuhn's words, 'normal science does not aim at novelties of fact or theory, and when successful finds none'. Above all, Kuhn stressed that normal scientists are not trying to test the paradigm. On the contrary, they accept the paradigm ③<u>critically</u>, and conduct their research within the limits it sets. If a normal scientist gets an experimental result which conflicts with the paradigm, they will usually assume that their experimental technique is ④<u>faulty</u>, not that the paradigm is wrong.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ 원문은 unquestioningly(의심 없이). 정상 과학자는 패러다임을 검증하지 않고 '의심 없이' 받아들인다는 맥락이므로 critically(비판적으로)는 부적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① eliminate — 정상 과학자의 일은 사소한 퍼즐을 '제거하는(eliminate)' 것이라는 맥락에 적절
❌ ② conservative — 정상 과학은 기존 패러다임을 발전·확장할 뿐인 '보수적(conservative)' 활동이라는 맥락에 적절
✅ ③ critically — 원문은 unquestioningly(의심 없이). 바로 앞에서 '정상 과학자는 패러다임을 검증하려 하지 않는다'고 했으므로 그들은 패러다임을 '의심 없이' 받아들인다. critically(비판적으로)로 바꾸면 정반대가 되어 부적절 ← 정답
❌ ④ faulty — 패러다임과 상충하는 결과가 나오면 자기 실험 기법이 '잘못됐다(faulty)'고 여긴다는 맥락에 적절
det.tip: 정상 과학자는 패러다임을 검증하려 하지 않으므로 they accept the paradigm unquestioningly(의심 없이)가 원문. critically는 정반대

questions.passage: Countershading is the process of optical flattening that provides camouflage to animals. When sunlight illuminates an object from above, the object will be brightest on top. The color of the object will gradually shade darker toward the bottom. This shading gives the object depth and allows the viewer to __________ its shape. Thus even if an animal is exactly, but uniformly, the same color as the substrate, it will be easily visible when illuminated. Most animals, however, are darker above than they are below. When they are illuminated from above, the darker back is lightened and the lighter belly is shaded. The animal thus appears to be a single color and easily blends in with the substrate. This pattern of coloration, or countershading, reduces the visual impression of shape in the organism. It allows the animal to blend in with its background.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: allows the viewer to distinguish its shape = 보는 이가 그 형태를 '구별하게' 한다
det.analysis:
❌ ① hide — '숨기다'. 음영이 형태를 드러내 '구별하게' 한다는 맥락과 반대
❌ ② enlarge — '확대하다'. 크기를 키운다는 뜻으로 형태 인식과 무관
❌ ③ ignore — '무시하다'. 형태를 알아보게 한다는 흐름과 반대
✅ ④ distinguish — '구별하다, 알아보다'. 음영이 물체에 깊이를 주어 보는 이가 그 '형태를 구별하게' 한다는 맥락에 정확히 부합 ← 정답
det.tip: shading gives the object depth and allows the viewer to distinguish its shape(형태를 구별)

questions.passage:
(A) The entrepreneur does not need to possess the <u>means</u> of production; they only need to recognise and act on opportunities.
(B) Entrepreneurs act on unexploited gain, which <u>means</u> that they are not just rational calculators but also risk-takers.
questions.stem: (A)와 (B)의 밑줄 친 means의 문맥상 의미로 가장 적절하게 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) the means of production = 생산 '수단'(명사), (B) which means = ~을 '의미하다'(동사)
det.analysis:
✅ ① (A) 수단·방법 / (B) 의미하다: (A) 'the means of production'은 생산 '수단'을 뜻하는 명사이고, (B) 'which means (that)'은 앞 내용이 '~을 의미한다'는 동사이므로 정확 ← 정답
❌ ② (A) 평균 / (B) 인색한: (A)를 '평균(mean)'으로 보면 생산 수단이라는 문맥과 어긋나고 (B)의 '인색한'도 문맥과 맞지 않음
❌ ③ (A) 의미하다 / (B) 수단·방법: 두 문맥의 품사·의미를 서로 뒤바꾼 오답
❌ ④ (A) 자원 / (B) 비열한: 두 문맥 모두와 맞지 않음
det.tip: the means of production(수단) vs which means that ~(의미하다)

questions.passage: In the past, it was often assumed that competence acquired in the first language (L1) was qualitatively different from that in a second language (L2) or any subsequent language. This privileging of the "native language" led to many popular misconceptions, such as believing that children of bilingual parents would never fully acquire either language, remaining somehow linguistically disadvantaged. Such claims are due to the belief that monolingualism is the norm, and they are held by many in the United States and other countries where a single language is politically or socially <u>dominant</u>. That this view must be wrong can easily be seen from the fact that many people in the world are speaking more than one language. In fact, it is bilingualism or trilingualism rather than monolingualism that is most common. Even in supposedly monolingual nations like the United States, U.S. Census figures from 2014 showed that at least 20 percent of the population regularly spoke a language other than English, and 53 percent of these people also spoke English.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 dominant와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: dominant = 지배적인 ↔ subordinate(종속적인)
det.analysis:
❌ ① powerful — '강력한'. dominant와 비슷한 뜻이라 반의어가 아님
✅ ② subordinate — '종속적인, 하위의'. 한 언어가 정치·사회적으로 '지배적(dominant)'이라는 것과 반대되는 뜻 ← 정답
❌ ③ prevailing — '우세한, 지배적인'. dominant의 유의어라 반대가 아님
❌ ④ superior — '우월한'. 지배적이라는 뜻과 가까워 반의어가 아님
det.tip: a single language is politically or socially dominant(지배적) ↔ subordinate(종속적)
